newsitem.title: NEPAL: Bodies of American trekkers brought to Kathmandu.
newsitem.headline: Bodies of American trekkers brought to Kathmandu.

text.p: The bodies of an American couple killed in a blizzard while on their way to a Buddhist monastery in western Nepal were brought to Kathmandu on Tuesday, members of a search team said.

Philip Jack Fialkow, 62, dean of a medical school in Seattle, Washington, and Helen Costas Fialkow, 61, were killed along with three Nepalese guides when their camp at 4,725 metres (15,500 feet) was hit by a blizzard in late October.
"I think they all died at the same time," said Kishendra Shahi, pilot of the helicopter which airlifted the bodies.
A search team on Sunday dug the bodies out from two-metre (yard) deep snow at Lumla, 450 km (281 miles) northwest of Kathmandu.
The couple were on their way to Tse Gomba, a popular Buddhist monastery in western Nepal.
A U.S. embassy official said the bodies would be kept at the mission's morgue in Kathmandu, pending a decision by the families whether to fly them to the United States.
